statement: Code PI is defined as a number unique to a patient within an Assigning Authority; code PT is the patient external identifier. Both are distinct codes from MR.
location: HL7 v2 table 0203, codes PI, PT
inference: Patient-level identifiers other than MR exist as separate typed roles; whether they share the MRN kind or need their own is project inference.

notes: No value format is stated; PT carries only a name-level definition.

statement: Code AN is defined as an identifier unique to an account; code VN is the visit number. Neither definition links the identifier to an individual.
location: HL7 v2 table 0203, codes AN, VN
inference: Account and visit numbers are typed identifier roles separate from MR; person linkage is not stated by the definitions.

notes: Person linkage of AN and VN alone is not established; no value format stated.

statement: Encounter.identifier is an optional repeating Identifier by which the encounter is known; the individual is linked through the separate Encounter.subject element.
location: FHIR R4 Encounter, elements identifier and subject
inference: An encounter id alone is not shown to identify an individual; person linkage is a separate element, as for claims and orders.

notes: No value format is stated; classification of a bare encounter id is unresolved.

statement: Account.identifier is an optional repeating Identifier described as the account number; the account links to a person through the separate Account.subject element and Account.type may be patient, expense or depreciation.
location: FHIR R4 Account, elements identifier, type and subject
inference: An account number is a financial or billing identifier whose health linkage depends on account type and holder; it is not shown to be a health-record identifier by itself.

notes: Account type varies; collisions with bank or utility account numbers are not source-addressed.

statement: Account numbers (paragraph (b)(2)(i)(J)) and any other unique identifying number, characteristic or code (paragraph (b)(2)(i)(R)) are listed among the identifiers removed for safe-harbor de-identification.
inference: Encounter, visit and facility-local identifiers fall under the catch-all (R) only when they are unique identifying codes; the list defines de-identification, not field semantics, and applies by holder.

notes: Holder-dependent applicability not settled; the list gives no format or label.
The catch-all (R) is not a statement that every local code is PHI.
